subject: Michael Jackson
clues: He began performing professionally before most children start school.
His signature move was inspired by a street dance style he saw in a music video.
He purchased the Beatles' song catalog in 1985 for roughly $47 million.
He lived on a private estate in California he named after a fictional place from a book.
His 1982 album remains the best-selling album of all time.
He was the lead vocalist of the Jackson 5 before his solo career made him the King of Pop.

subject: The Shining
clues: The author of the source novel hated this adaptation so much he later made his own version.
The hedge maze in the film does not exist in the original book.
Exactly 127 takes were demanded for one particular scene involving a door.
A famous carpet pattern from this film became an academic subject of analysis.
Jack Nicholson plays a writer who slowly loses his mind in an isolated mountain hotel.
Stanley Kubrick directed this 1980 horror film based on a Stephen King novel.
Air traffic across an entire continent was grounded within hours of the first strike.
The phone calls made from the planes changed how hijackings are responded to forever.
A field in Pennsylvania became a crash site after passengers fought back against the hijackers.
Both towers had been attacked before — a truck bomb in the basement, years earlier.
Nearly 3,000 people died in attacks on New York and Washington on the same morning.
On September 11, 2001, al-Qaeda hijackers flew commercial planes into the World Trade Center.

subject: The Amazon River
clues: It discharges more fresh water into the ocean than any other river on Earth.
Its mouth is so wide that early explorers did not realize it was a river.
Some stretches have no bridge crossing them despite running through multiple countries.
Pink dolphins are among the species found only in its basin.
It flows through the largest tropical rainforest on the planet.
This South American river is the largest by water volume in the world.

subject: Pablo Picasso
clues: His full baptismal name contained 23 words.
He kept the full name of the woman who inspired his most politically charged painting secret for years.
He was questioned by police after the Mona Lisa was stolen — he had bought stolen art from the same thief.
He created over 20,000 works across painting, sculpture, ceramics, and printmaking.
His 1937 painting depicting a bombing in the Basque Country became the most famous anti-war artwork ever made.
This Spanish artist co-founded Cubism and painted Guernica.

subject: Titanic
clues: A lifeboat drill scheduled for the morning of the sinking was cancelled.
The ship received six iceberg warnings the day it sank — none caused a course change.
A nearby ship saw the distress flares but did not respond in time.
Third-class passengers were physically prevented from reaching the upper decks.
Over 1,500 people died when it sank on its maiden voyage in April 1912.
The RMS Titanic struck an iceberg and sank in the North Atlantic on its first journey.

subject: Bob Dylan
clues: He changed his name before recording his first album, borrowing it from a Welsh poet.
He was booed by his own audience when he plugged in an electric guitar for the first time.
His manager famously refused to let him appear on The Ed Sullivan Show over a song choice.
He accepted his Nobel Prize in Literature months late and sent someone else to collect it.
His 1965 song 'Like a Rolling Stone' changed what a pop single was allowed to be.
This American singer-songwriter won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016.

subject: The Colosseum
clues: It was built using labor and materials seized after the sacking of Jerusalem.
Its retractable awning system required 1,000 sailors to operate.
It could be flooded to stage mock naval battles.
It held between 50,000 and 80,000 spectators and had 80 entrance arches.
Gladiatorial combat and public executions were held here for four centuries.
This ancient Roman amphitheater in the center of Rome is the largest ever built.

subject: Frida Kahlo
clues: She contracted polio at age six, leaving one leg thinner than the other.
She began painting seriously while bedridden after a bus accident shattered her spine.
She married the same man twice — each time the relationship was marked by mutual infidelity.
Her unibrow and traditional Tehuana dress were deliberate political statements.
More than a third of her 143 paintings are self-portraits.
This Mexican painter is one of the most recognizable artists of the 20th century.

subject: The Moon Landing
clues: A president prepared a speech in advance in case the astronauts did not make it back.
The computer guiding the landing had less processing power than a modern pocket calculator.
One astronaut remained alone in the orbiting module while the others descended.
The mission was named after the Greek god of the sun.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent 21 hours on the lunar surface in July 1969.
Apollo 11 landed humans on the Moon for the first time on July 20, 1969.

subject: Pulp Fiction
clues: Its timeline is deliberately scrambled — the last scene chronologically appears near the middle.
A $5 milkshake becomes a point of serious conversation between two hitmen.
John Travolta's career was considered finished before this film brought him back.
It won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and lost the Oscar to Forrest Gump.
Uma Thurman plays a gangster's wife who nearly dies of a drug overdose.
Quentin Tarantino directed this 1994 crime anthology film.

subject: Charles Darwin
clues: He originally trained to become a clergyman before science consumed him.
He spent five years on a naval survey ship, collecting specimens across South America and the Pacific.
He sat on his theory for 20 years before publishing, fearing the reaction.
A letter from a fellow naturalist with the same idea forced him to finally publish.
His 1859 book introduced the mechanism of natural selection to explain species change.
This English naturalist wrote On the Origin of Species.

subject: Chernobyl
clues: The explosion was partly caused by a safety test that was supposed to make the reactor safer.
An entire city of 50,000 people was evacuated with three hours notice and never resettled.
The first responders were not told what they were walking into.
A so-called 'liquidator' workforce of 600,000 was deployed over years to contain the damage.
A 2019 HBO miniseries dramatized the disaster and the Soviet government's cover-up.
Reactor No. 4 at a Ukrainian nuclear plant exploded in April 1986 in the world's worst nuclear accident.

subject: Hamlet
clues: It is the most performed play in history and has been translated into every written language.
The ghost appears in the first scene — before the protagonist does.
It contains more famous quotes than almost any other single work in English.
The play within the play is used as a trap to catch a murderer.
A Danish prince's decision to avenge his father's murder drives the entire plot.
This is Shakespeare's longest play and one of the most analyzed works in literary history.

subject: Usain Bolt
clues: He ate McDonald's chicken nuggets every day at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
He celebrated before crossing the finish line in his world record 100m run and still set the record.
He is 6'5" — considered too tall by coaches who said he would never be a sprinter.
He won three gold medals at three consecutive Olympics.
His world record of 9.58 seconds in the 100m has stood since 2009.
This Jamaican sprinter is the fastest human ever recorded.

subject: The Great Fire of London
clues: It started in a bakery on Pudding Lane in the early hours of the morning.
Only six deaths were officially recorded, though historians believe the real number was higher.
It destroyed 13,200 houses and 87 churches across four days.
The fire created the conditions for Christopher Wren to rebuild the city's skyline.
It effectively ended the plague that had been killing Londoners for the previous year.
This catastrophic fire burned through the medieval city of London in September 1666.

subject: Netflix
clues: It started as a DVD-by-mail service with no late fees — a direct attack on Blockbuster.
Blockbuster was offered the chance to buy it for $50 million and declined.
It began producing its own content after a Danish political drama showed it was possible.
Its recommendation algorithm was the subject of a million-dollar public competition.
It went from mailing DVDs to becoming the world's dominant streaming service.
This American company redefined how television and film are distributed and consumed globally.

subject: Marie Curie
clues: She had to sit behind a screen at scientific conferences because women were not officially allowed.
She was the first person — not first woman, first person — to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
Her notebooks are still radioactive and are stored in lead-lined boxes.
She personally drove ambulances equipped with X-ray machines to the front lines in World War I.
She discovered two new elements: polonium, named after her homeland, and radium.
This Polish-French physicist was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.

subject: The Dark Knight
clues: Heath Ledger locked himself in a hotel room for six weeks to prepare for his role.
An IMAX camera was destroyed during the filming of the bank robbery scene.
The actor playing the villain died before the film was released.
It was the first superhero film to be taken seriously as a crime drama.
The Joker becomes Gotham's primary threat as Batman tries to hold the city together.
Christopher Nolan directed this 2008 Batman film, widely considered one of the greatest superhero films ever made.

subject: Pompeii
clues: Its residents had no concept or word for what a volcano was — they thought it was a mountain.
Plaster casts of its victims were made by filling the voids their bodies left in hardened ash.
Intact election graffiti on its walls shows campaigns that were still running when the city died.
A fast food street culture with over 80 thermopoliae — ancient snack bars — has been excavated.
It was buried so quickly that loaves of bread were found still in ovens.
This Roman city near Naples was buried under volcanic ash by Vesuvius in 79 AD and preserved almost perfectly.

subject: The Beatles
clues: They were rejected by every major record label in London before signing with a small classical imprint.
Their last live performance was on a rooftop in London — unannounced, in the middle of a workday.
They spent more studio time on one album than the entire first decade of rock and roll combined.
John Lennon was arrested in Hamburg for arson before they were famous.
They appeared on The Ed Sullivan Show in 1964 to an audience of 73 million people.
This British band from Liverpool is the best-selling music act in history.

subject: Avatar
clues: Its director spent years developing technology that didn't yet exist before he could make it.
It was rejected by every studio before one agreed to fund it — on the condition it was scaled back.
The language spoken by its alien species was created by a professional linguist.
It held the record as the highest-grossing film of all time for a decade.
A planet called Pandora and its indigenous Na'vi people are at the center of the story.
James Cameron directed this 2009 science fiction film, the highest-grossing film ever made at the time.

subject: The Eiffel Tower
clues: It was supposed to be demolished after 20 years but was saved because it made a useful radio antenna.
It grows taller in summer — thermal expansion adds up to 15cm in the heat.
Its original color was reddish-brown — it has been repainted in a yellow-brown shade 19 times since.
Over 300 workers and 18,038 pieces of iron were used to build it in just over two years.
When it was built in 1889, it was the tallest man-made structure in the world.
This iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris is the most visited paid monument on Earth.

subject: Ayrton Senna
clues: He once lapped an entire field in wet conditions at Monaco in a race that was later red-flagged.
He described entering a trance-like state while driving, which frightened him enough to lift off.
His rivalry with Alain Prost ended with them deliberately colliding twice in championship deciders.
He died at a corner called Tamburello at Imola — a crash watched live on television across the world.
He won three Formula 1 World Championships despite driving for a less dominant team in two of them.
This Brazilian racing driver is widely considered the greatest Formula 1 driver of all time.
It was written while the author was dying of tuberculosis on a remote Scottish island.
The author submitted it under a different title — his publisher changed it.
Its appendix is written in past tense — implying the regime it depicts eventually fell.
It invented words that entered everyday language: doublethink, thoughtcrime, unperson.
Big Brother watches a man named Winston Smith who begins secretly rebelling against a totalitarian state.
George Orwell wrote this 1949 novel, one of the most influential dystopias ever written.

subject: Lionel Messi
clues: He was diagnosed with a growth hormone deficiency at 10 — Barcelona paid for his treatment in exchange for signing him.
He scored all five goals in a Champions League match against Bayer Leverkusen in 2012.
He retired from international football after losing the 2016 Copa América final — then came back.
He won the Ballon d'Or eight times — more than any other footballer in history.
He finally won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022 after three previous final appearances.
This Argentine footballer is widely considered the greatest player in the history of the sport.

subject: Hiroshima
clues: The city was specifically chosen because it had not yet been bombed — to measure the weapon's full effect.
Shadows of vaporized people were burned permanently into walls and steps.
A wristwatch recovered from the rubble stopped at 8:15 a.m. — the exact moment of detonation.
Survivors of both Hiroshima and Nagasaki faced discrimination in Japan for decades afterward.
The bomb was dropped from a B-29 named Enola Gay, after the pilot's mother.
An atomic bomb was dropped on this Japanese city on August 6, 1945, killing over 70,000 people instantly.

subject: The Louvre
clues: It was a royal fortress and prison before it became a museum during the French Revolution.
It takes nine months to walk past every work in its collection if you spend 30 seconds on each.
Napoleon used one of its grand halls as his private apartment.
Its controversial glass pyramid entrance was deeply hated when it opened in 1989.
It is home to the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo, and the Winged Victory of Samothrace.
This museum in Paris is the most visited art museum in the world.

subject: Muhammad Ali
clues: He threw his Olympic gold medal into a river after being refused service at a whites-only restaurant.
He was stripped of his heavyweight title and banned from boxing for three years for refusing the Vietnam draft.
He predicted the round his opponent would fall in — and was correct so often it became expected.
His fight with Joe Frazier in Manila in 1975 is considered the most brutal boxing match ever recorded.
He lit the Olympic flame at the Atlanta Games in 1996, his hands visibly trembling from Parkinson's.
Born Cassius Clay, this American boxer is widely considered the greatest heavyweight of all time.

subject: Fairuz
clues: She was discovered singing in a government radio choir as a teenager in Beirut.
Her morning broadcasts became a ritual — entire cities would stop to listen.
She refused to perform during the Lebanese Civil War, saying she would only sing for a united Lebanon.
She collaborated with the Rahbani brothers for decades, one of whom she married.
Her voice became so synonymous with Lebanon that she is called the country's ambassador to the stars.
This Lebanese singer is considered the greatest Arab vocalist of the 20th century.

subject: Chichen Itza
clues: During the spring and autumn equinoxes, a shadow shaped like a serpent descends its main pyramid.
Its ballcourt is the largest in the ancient Americas — losers may have been ritually sacrificed.
It was not fully excavated until the 20th century, though it had been a tourist destination for Spanish conquistadors.
Its main pyramid has 365 steps — one for each day of the solar calendar.
It was a major city of the Maya civilization in what is now Mexico.
This ancient Mayan city in the Yucatán Peninsula is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
